scan_cadence.premarket: ~20 minutes, NOT the protocol's 5 minutes. Logged as a deliberate deviation per SCAN ECONOMY rule 5 rather than left to be inferred.
scan_cadence.reason: Two constraints bind. (1) HEADLESS SINGLE-TURN: the whole day runs inside one turn, so every tool call spends wall clock that the 09:30-14:30 tradeable window needs; a true 5-minute premarket cadence from 06:30 is ~36 cycles and would consume the session. (2) Premarket entries are structurally near-impossible anyway - the parity audit records a ~90-100pct premarket spread-veto rate, and the Day-17/18 tick-size finding makes the 0.50pct cap a near-binary 1-tick test on sub-$4 names.
scan_cadence.post_open: Tighten to the protocol 5-minute cadence from 09:25 while FLAT with tickets remaining, because 09:30 collapses spreads and that is where entries actually become possible.
scan_cadence.in_position: Drop scan duty to a ~20-minute light bench refresh; the 1-minute position watch owns the cadence and must never be starved (API HYGIENE #3).
scan_cadence.honesty_note: This deviation makes the premarket half of the day a LOWER-discovery process than the champion's. Direction of bias is under-discovery of late-premarket crossers, not over-trading.

spread.MARGINAL: REFUSED BY ONE TICK. At $4.10 a $0.01 tick is 0.244pct of price, so the 0.50pct cap admits exactly TWO ticks (0.488pct) and no more. The book showed THREE (4.07 / 4.10). spread.sizing_20pct_rule: NOT BINDING by a wide margin - the trailing 10 completed minutes allowed 81,676 shares against 3,658 intended.

spread.veto_rate_significance: This is exactly the divergence the parity audit is trying to price. The sim has NO spread veto - it would have taken this trade and paid a haircut. Live refused it on a one-tick difference. Logged in the POST-OPEN bucket, which is the one the V-series says should be running at 50-65pct and where Day 8 measured 40pct.
spread.not_a_chase_note: Recorded separately: by 09:38 price had ALSO taken out both the ORB high 4.0380 and the premarket high 4.0500, so a Trigger A or B stop-buy at either level would have been a met trigger and refused by the fill-arming rule as a disguised market order. spread.context: TRIGGER A ratchet - the ORB high 4.0380 and the premarket high 4.0500 were both taken out in the 09:36-09:38 push, so the ratchet moved up to the new RTH session high 4.1000. Stop-buy at 4.1000, limit 4.1205.

spread.fill_arming: PASS - last 4.0724 and bid 4.07 are both below the 4.1000 ratchet trigger, so this is a legitimate forward stop and not a disguised market order. spread.distinct_from_the_09_38_veto: Logged as a SEPARATE decision because it is a different trigger (A ratchet stop-buy vs C pattern marketable limit) at a different level (4.1000 vs 4.1123) on a re-quoted book - not a second reading of the same evaluation.

spread.context: TRIGGER A ratchet moved again to the new RTH session high 4.1400 (from 4.1000 a minute earlier). Stop-buy at 4.1400, limit 4.1607.
spread.fill_arming: PASS - last 4.0450 is 2.3pct below the 4.1400 ratchet trigger, a clean forward stop.
spread.tick_size_arithmetic: At $4.07 one tick is 0.246pct, so the 0.50pct cap admits exactly TWO ticks (0.491pct). NEOV has now shown 3, 4, 4 and 3 ticks across four consecutive evaluations - it keeps sitting one tick outside the cap.
spread.veto_counting_convention_ADOPTED_HERE: A veto DECISION is counted when (a) a fresh Trigger C prints, or (b) the ratchet level MOVES, i.e. whenever there is a genuinely new level to arm. Re-checking an unchanged level is MONITORING and is not counted again. Without this the veto rate would measure my polling frequency rather than the strategy's refusal rate, which would corrupt exactly the calibration the parity audit needs.

negative_book_flag_UNRESOLVED_but_moot.observation: pb_ratio -6.0978, i.e. deeply negative book value, against a reported loan_pct of only 5.33 (~$16.8M of debt on a $315.6M cap) and cash_pct 9.29 (~$29.3M).
negative_book_flag_UNRESOLVED_but_moot.why_it_is_suspicious_here_specifically: A GPU-cloud operator finances its fleet. If a material part of that sits in finance/operating LEASE obligations rather than in the 'loans' line the screen reads, loan_pct would understate real leverage - and deeply negative book value is exactly the symptom that pattern produces. This is a sharper concern than generic negative book, because the business model predicts the specific liability the screen might miss.
negative_book_flag_UNRESOLVED_but_moot.compared_to_precedent: Distinguished from YDES (the protocol's named implausible-input case) because YDES reported loan_pct EXACTLY 0.00; MOVE reports 5.33 and 9.29, both non-zero. negative_book_flag_UNRESOLVED_but_moot.status: NOT RESOLVED, and deliberately not resolved, because it cannot change any decision today - see calm_gap below. Recording it as an open question rather than either burying it or over-refusing on it.

calm_gap.verdict: FAIL - and permanently, for the entire session
calm_gap.reason: MOVE's first real print of 2026-08-31 was 11:45Z = 07:45 ET. There is no 07:00 ET bar on Robinhood or on Polygon, so gap7 is n/a, and the ranker fails conservative on a missing gap7 by design.
calm_gap.structural_consequence: Because gap7 is anchored to a fixed 07:00 clock time, a name that STARTS trading after 07:00 can never acquire one. MOVE is therefore unarmable for the whole day no matter how it trades - it was +23.9pct at 07:51 and +34.6pct three minutes later, on 22,417 shares in a single minute, and none of that can make it eligible.
calm_gap.is_this_right: Following the tool rather than arguing with it, per the standing rule that the rank command wins over hand judgement. But flagging it as a genuine structural question for review: the calm-gap gate exists to refuse names that have ALREADY RUN too far by 7AM, and a name that had not yet traded at 7AM is a different case from one that gapped 60pct by then. Today it costs nothing to be strict; on another day it could refuse a clean late-opening name.

PAVS.reverse_split_note: 52-week high 148,800.00 against a 3.76 low, pb_ratio 0.001457, 857,138 shares outstanding - an extremely heavily reverse-split shell. avg_volume_2_weeks 32,747 vs avg_volume_30_days 1,620,890.

YARW.detail: Yarrow Bioscience, $98.8M clinical-stage biotech developing YB-101, an antibody therapy for Graves disease and thyroid eye disease, New Haven CT, 10 employees, founded October 2025. Permissible business (pharmaceuticals). Refused on question 1: a pre-revenue biotech sitting on cash worth 26.68pct of its market cap breaches CASH>10 + COMBINED>20. The one-side carve-out cannot help - it requires combined <= 20 and combined is 26.68.
YARW.zero_loan_check: loan_pct is EXACTLY 0.00, which is the input that triggers the YDES implausibility test. Checked and DISTINGUISHED: YDES paired a 0.00 loan with NEGATIVE book value (pb -0.811), which is internally contradictory. YARW reports pb_ratio +1.12, i.e. positive book - a debt-free clinical-stage biotech that raised equity and holds the proceeds is entirely plausible with zero debt. Not an implausible input, and it FAILS on the cash side regardless.
YARW.third_biotech_of_the_day_refused_the_sam: CNTB (cash 32.93), YARW (cash 26.68) and APMD on Day 18 (cash 24.91) are the same structural refusal: a pre-revenue drug developer holding a large cash pile relative to a small market cap. The gate is not making a judgement about biotech; the arithmetic of cash/mcap simply lands above 10 for this whole class.

SAIC.q1: FAIL. loan 50.25 with combined 52.3 against a 20 cap. The cash side is clean at 2.05 - this is an ordinary investment-grade corporate balance sheet, and the ratio test refuses it precisely because a real operating company carries real debt.
SAIC.q2: FAIL. Science Applications International Corp provides technical, engineering and enterprise IT services for large complex GOVERNMENT projects. Its own description names its key customers as the Department of Defense (first), NASA, State, Justice, Homeland Security and 'several sensitive intelligence community agencies'. 23,000 employees, Reston VA, founded 1969.
SAIC.amd_principle_considered_and_rejected: This is the decisive reasoning, so it is recorded in full. The AMD principle rescues a GENERAL-PURPOSE product sold INTO a defence market; it does not rescue a DEDICATED vertical supplier to that market. SAIC does not sell a general-purpose product that defence happens to buy - it exists to build and operate systems FOR the defence and intelligence community, and essentially all of its revenue is US government contracting. That is the same call already made twice in this campaign: CRD.A on Day 18 (dedicated insurance-industry claims service, not rescued) and TP on Day 18 (dedicated live-entertainment ticketing platform, not rescued).
SAIC.civil_agencies_do_not_save_it: NASA, State and Justice work is permissible in itself, so the company is not 100pct defence. But under the BINARY 5pct rule the haram share must be shown to be UNDER 5pct, and there is no disclosure splitting defence/intelligence revenue out - it is plainly the main line, not a 5pct remainder. Absence of evidence is never compliance.
SAIC.significance: THE COST-OF-THE-GATE OBSERVATION OF THE DAY, and the sharpest instance of the Day-8 structural tension so far this campaign. SAIC is a $5.32B company with 431k average daily volume and a 52-week-high breakout - by an order of magnitude the most liquid and tightest-book name to cross +10pct today, and the only one whose book could have absorbed a full $15,000 ticket without any depth concern at all. It is refused twice over. Every name the strategy can actually trade today is a sub-$200M microcap.
SAIC.note_on_ordering: Both refusals are independent and either alone is sufficient. Recording both rather than stopping at the first, because the question-2 reasoning is the one that would generalise to a future SAIC-like name whose leverage happened to be clean.

findings.what: EOSEW - 'Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc. Warrant' - crossed +18.18% at 3.25 and landed in the candidate pool as an ordinary name. It is neither a fund nor a SPAC, so neither FUND_PAT nor SPAC_PAT dropped it, yet C37 eligibility requires COMMON STOCK. Nothing in the pipeline was checking that.
findings.why_it_matters: Two independent failures, not one. (1) Eligibility: a warrant is not common stock and was never tradeable under the protocol. (2) The ranker would have mis-measured it anyway - a warrant's prev_close, coil and premarket high are derivative of the underlying's tape, so its gain%, coil and 30-bar pressure are not comparable to a common-stock crosser's, and it would have competed for the TOP slot on numbers that mean something different.
findings.fix: Added NONCOMMON_PAT to plan/scan_sweep.py with its own 'noncommon' drop bucket, covering warrants, rights, units, preferreds/depositary shares, debentures and notes. Verified on the 06:31 dump: EOSEW now drops mechanically and the candidate count fell 15 -> 14. Preferreds are included for the same eligibility reason and are additionally fixed-income in substance, which is a live halal question of its own.
findings.why_mechanical: The alternative was to remember to exclude EOSEW by hand on every cycle for the rest of the day. That is precisely the hand-ranking drift the rank command exists to prevent, so the fix belongs in the tool, not in my attention.

findings.what: BESS, CTW, EDRY, ANPA and HVT.A each returned 145 INTERPOLATED bars and ZERO real ones from get_equity_historicals - they had not traded premarket at all, so their scan %Change is a stale mark rather than a live move.
findings.detector: The Day-8 all-interpolated-bars detector, working exactly as designed. rh_bars_ingest.py skipped every bar and the ranker excluded all five as 'NO BARS (fetch first)'.
findings.note: HVT.A is doubly untradeable: 2,004 shares in the prior session against the 20pct-of-10-min-volume sizing rule. It is also a dotted Class-A ticker, the same shape as CRD.A on Day 18 whose ratios were UNVERIFIABLE in yfinance.
findings.caveat: fake_gap was deliberately RESET at seeding rather than inherited - a name dark premarket yesterday may trade today - so these five are not permanently dropped. They are excluded for want of bars, and a real print later today puts them back in the pool.

findings.severity: discovery-integrity defect - inflates the crossed set with crosses that never printed
findings.what: For names with no premarket tape, the scanner's 'Last' column is an indicative/stale mark rather than a traded price, so its %Change describes a move that did not happen. Four cases today, each verified against the real 1-minute bars:

evidence.CTW: scan Last 2.90 vs prev_close 2.58 = +12.40pct. Real tape: no trades at all, flat interpolated series at 2.55. Against 2.58 that is -1.2pct - the name is DOWN, not up 12pct.
evidence.CNTB: scan Last 2.4995 = +12.09pct. Real tape: one print at 11:00Z, 1,000 shares at 2.32 = +4.0pct vs prev_close 2.23. Never crossed +10pct.
evidence.EDRY: scan Last 57.15 = +13.45pct. Real tape: one print at 11:00Z, 155 shares at 53.00 = +5.2pct vs prev_close 50.375. Never crossed +10pct.
evidence.CVR: scan Last 12.00 = +17.19pct. Real tape: zero trades, flat interpolated at 10.04. Never crossed +10pct.

findings.why_it_matters: The crossed-set LATCH exists because the champion treats a +10pct cross as permanent once it has PRINTED. These four never printed one. Latching them makes the live universe larger than the champion's in a way that is invisible in the ledger - the exact mirror of divergence #2 in the parity audit, which corrects the opposite error (under-discovery when a real crosser fades off the snapshot).
findings.did_it_cost_anything_today: No. All four were excluded downstream anyway - the ranker refused them as NO BARS or too-few-bars, so none could have been armed. The defect is currently masked by the fake-gap detector rather than handled on its own terms.
findings.handling: Deliberately did NOT purge them from the crossed set. Dropping a latched name is under-discovery, and fake_gap is reset daily precisely because a name dark at 07:00 may trade later - if any of these prints a genuine +10pct cross during RTH it becomes eligible on its own tape. They stay latched but unarmable, and the ranker keeps refusing them until real bars exist.
findings.recommended_followup: The clean fix is to gate the LATCH on a real print rather than on the scanner's %Change: only add a name to the crossed set once its own bars show a >=+10pct trade vs prev_close. That is a change to the discovery contract, so it belongs in a reviewed patch rather than a mid-session edit - logged here rather than done today.

findings.loud_log: GAP7 COMPLETION ATTEMPTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED - MOVE.
findings.trigger_for_the_attempt: The ranker put MOVE at rank 1 (coil 0.926, pressure +0.35, halal PASS) but read gap7 = n/a and therefore CALM-GAP FAIL. That is the standing instruction's exact case: an RH-premarket-dark name failing for a DATA reason rather than a market reason, which must be completed from shared.massive.minute_bars (Polygon) rather than silently accepted.
findings.what_the_completion_found: Polygon returned ZERO bars for MOVE on 2026-08-31. Control probes on the same call path returned full tapes for SPY (148 bars) and NEOV (142 bars), so the feed was healthy and the empty result is about MOVE, not about Polygon.
findings.the_actual_explanation: MOVE's FIRST REAL PRINT OF THE DAY was 11:45Z = 07:45 ET (721 shares at 11.97-14.00). It did not trade at 07:00 ET on Robinhood OR on Polygon. There is no 7AM bar to complete because the stock had not started trading yet.
findings.verdict: CALM-GAP FAIL STANDS, and it is REAL rather than a data artefact. The completion tool did its job by refusing to manufacture a gap7 that never existed. Recording the attempt loudly, as required, precisely because the honest outcome here was 'no rescue'.
findings.secondary_check: Even taken at its first print, MOVE would be +4.2pct (11.97 vs prev_close 11.49) - but its CURRENT gain is +34.6pct and rising fast (16.71 high inside six minutes), so the name is running away from the gate, not sitting quietly under it.
findings.cross_validation_bonus: The same probe independently confirmed NEOV's gap7: Polygon's 07:00 ET close 3.7001 vs prev_close 3.34 = +10.78pct, against RH's +10.8pct. Two independent feeds agreeing on the gate input for the day's only armable name is worth more than the MOVE result.

findings.what: At 07:54 ET the Polygon minute tape ended at 07:38 ET for BOTH control symbols (SPY last=07:38, NEOV last=07:38). That is a consistent ~15-16 minute lag, not a per-symbol gap.
findings.why_it_matters: It bounds what the gap7-completion tool can do. Polygon can complete a 07:00 ET gap for any name checked after roughly 07:15, which covers the intended use. It CANNOT be used to adjudicate anything inside the last ~15 minutes - and a name that starts trading inside that window (exactly MOVE today) will look like 'no data' when it is really 'not yet delivered'.
findings.consequence_avoided: Without the SPY/NEOV controls, MOVE's empty Polygon result would have read as a broken feed or as evidence the stock was dark all morning. It was neither. Always run a control symbol before drawing a conclusion from an empty market-data response.
findings.unchanged: This does not affect live decisions, which are made on RH bars by bar policy. Polygon is used here only to answer a historical yes/no about a 07:00 print.

findings.what: Robinhood reports NEOV's premarket high as 4.0500, set on the 08:00Z (04:00 ET) bar with 11,753 shares. Polygon reports the premarket high over the same 04:00-07:38 ET window as 3.9800. A 1.76pct disagreement on the same symbol, same session, same minute.
findings.why_it_matters: The premarket high IS the Trigger B entry level. Using Polygon's 3.98 instead of RH's 4.05 would have set a trigger 1.76pct lower - materially more likely to fill, on a name where the entry decision was live this morning. That is a decision-changing feed difference, not a cosmetic one.
findings.what_was_done: Used RH's 4.0500. Bar policy is explicit that live decisions are made on Robinhood bars, and feed-calibration fix #8 forbids mixing a threshold derived on one feed with data from another. The trigger recorded in the veto ledger is the RH one.
findings.direction_of_bias: RH's higher premarket high makes our Trigger B STRICTER than a Polygon-based one would be, so this cuts toward fewer entries, not toward flattering fills.
findings.relation_to_prior_finding: This is the price-level cousin of the known ~4x premarket VOLUME disagreement between the two feeds (WDFC 2026-07-10). Volume divergence was already documented; a divergence in the HIGH - which is an entry trigger, not a statistic - had not been.
